_comment: CurriculumOS V1 genesis seed. Curated foundational concepts from open educational resources (OpenStax). Each kernel's anchored quotes are verified by the foundry's mechanical anchor check against the sourceSnapshots below before admission. Scaling to the full ~50-title library is the next foundry run.

sourceSnapshots.openstax:microeconomics-3e#5: Price elasticity of demand measures the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price; it is computed as the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price. Demand is described as elastic when the absolute value of the elasticity is greater than one, meaning quantity responds proportionally more than price. Demand is inelastic when the absolute value is less than one. Necessities tend to have inelastic demand because consumers have few substitutes, while luxuries tend to have elastic demand. The availability of close substitutes is a primary determinant of elasticity.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:microeconomics-3e#3: A demand curve shows the quantity of a good that consumers are willing and able to purchase at each price, holding all other factors constant. Demand curves typically slope downward, reflecting the law of demand: as price falls, quantity demanded rises. A change in price causes a movement along the demand curve, whereas a change in income, tastes, or the price of related goods shifts the entire curve.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:statistics#7: A sampling distribution is the probability distribution of a statistic obtained from a large number of samples drawn from a specific population. The central limit theorem states that the sampling distribution of the sample mean approaches a normal distribution as the sample size increases, regardless of the shape of the population distribution. The standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean is the population standard deviation divided by the square root of the sample size.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:statistics#9: A p-value is the probability of obtaining a test statistic at least as extreme as the one observed, assuming the null hypothesis is true. A small p-value indicates that the observed data would be unlikely under the null hypothesis. The p-value is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true, and it does not measure the size of an effect.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:biology-2e#8: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose. The light-dependent reactions capture energy from sunlight to produce ATP and NADPH, which the Calvin cycle then uses to fix carbon dioxide into sugar. Oxygen is released as a byproduct of splitting water molecules.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:biology-2e#3: The cell membrane, also called the plasma membrane, is a selectively permeable barrier that regulates which substances enter and leave the cell. It is composed of a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins. The membrane maintains the internal environment of the cell while allowing the exchange of nutrients and wastes.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:chemistry-2e#13: Chemical equilibrium is the state in which the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal, so the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant over time. Equilibrium is dynamic: both the forward and reverse reactions continue to occur even though no net change is observed. According to Le Chatelier's principle, when a system at equilibrium is disturbed by a change in concentration, temperature, or pressure, the equilibrium shifts in the direction that partially counteracts the disturbance.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:microeconomics-3e#4: Market equilibrium occurs at the price where the quantity demanded by buyers equals the quantity supplied by sellers. At this equilibrium price the opposing pressures of demand and supply are balanced and there is no tendency for the price to change. When the price is above equilibrium a surplus pushes it down, and when the price is below equilibrium a shortage pushes it up, so the market mechanism restores the balance.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:biology-2e#33: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a stable internal environment despite changes in external conditions. Most homeostatic systems rely on negative feedback, in which a change in a regulated variable triggers a response that counteracts the change and returns the variable toward its set point. Sensors detect the deviation, a control center compares it to the set point, and effectors produce a corrective response. The regulation of body temperature is a classic example of negative feedback homeostasis.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:macroeconomics-2e#11: A wage-price spiral is a self-reinforcing cycle in which rising prices lead workers to demand higher wages, and the higher wage costs lead firms to raise prices further. This is an example of positive feedback, in which an initial change is amplified rather than damped. Unlike negative feedback, positive feedback drives the system further from where it started.
sourceSnapshots.historical-thinking:reference: A historical argument is an interpretation of the past supported by evidence drawn from primary sources. Historians construct claims and justify them with evidence, using contextual reasoning to connect the sources to the interpretation. Every historical argument is bounded by the limitations of the surviving record, which is always incomplete and shaped by who created and preserved the sources.
sourceSnapshots.writing-about-literature:reference: Literary analysis advances an interpretive claim about a text and supports it with specific textual evidence. A strong interpretation uses close reading to explain how particular details produce meaning, rather than merely asserting a reading. Because texts are open to multiple interpretations, a careful argument acknowledges alternative readings the same evidence could support.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:microeconomics-3e#6: Consumer choice theory models how a consumer maximizes utility subject to a budget constraint. The consumer selects the affordable bundle of goods that yields the highest satisfaction. At the optimal choice, utility cannot be increased without exceeding the budget, so the consumer faces a tradeoff between goods.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:biology-2e#45: Optimal foraging theory models an animal as maximizing its net energy gain subject to the constraints of time and predation risk. The forager is predicted to choose the diet or patch that yields the greatest energy return per unit of time. Because time spent on one food item cannot be spent on another, foraging involves a tradeoff.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:microeconomics-3e#1: An economic model is a simplified representation of reality that keeps the features relevant to a question and discards the rest. Models such as supply and demand make assumptions, like rational choice or perfect competition, that do not hold exactly. A model is useful when its assumptions are close enough for the question at hand, and misleading when a key assumption breaks.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:statistics#12: A statistical model is a simplified mathematical representation of how data are generated. A model such as linear regression keeps a few structural features and discards others, relying on assumptions like linearity and independent errors. When those assumptions fail, the model's conclusions can be misleading even if it fits the sample well.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:biology-2e#7: Cellular respiration is a staged process that releases energy from glucose through an ordered sequence: glycolysis, the citric acid cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation. Each stage depends on the products of the previous one; the citric acid cycle uses the pyruvate produced by glycolysis, and oxidative phosphorylation uses the electron carriers generated by the earlier stages. Blocking an earlier stage halts the later ones.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:chemistry-2e#4: A titration is a staged laboratory procedure for determining an unknown concentration: standardize the titrant, add it gradually to the analyte while monitoring, and identify the endpoint at the equivalence point. Each step depends on the previous one; an unstandardized titrant makes the endpoint reading meaningless. Performing steps out of order invalidates the result. The law of conservation of mass states that matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction, so the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products. Balancing a chemical equation enforces this law: the number of atoms of each element must be equal on both sides of the equation. Coefficients are adjusted to balance an equation, never subscripts, because changing a subscript would change the identity of the substance.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:statistics#1: An observational study measures variables without assigning treatments, so an association it finds may be due to a confounding variable rather than a causal effect. A confounding variable influences both the supposed cause and the supposed effect, creating a spurious association. Establishing causation generally requires ruling out confounders, often through a randomized experiment.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:macroeconomics-2e#2: A natural experiment uses a policy change or external event that affects one group but not another to estimate a causal effect from observational data. The credibility of the causal claim depends on whether the two groups were comparable apart from the change, so that the difference can be attributed to the policy rather than to a confounding factor.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:macroeconomics-2e#1: In the circular flow of income, money that households earn returns to firms as spending unless it leaks out of the flow as saving, taxes, or spending on imports. Leakages are balanced by injections such as investment, government spending, and exports that add spending back into the flow. When total leakages equal total injections, the circular flow is in balance and national income neither rises nor falls.

facts.text: Coefficients are adjusted to balance an equation, never subscripts, because changing a subscript would change the identity of the substance.

anchor.quote: Coefficients are adjusted to balance an equation, never subscripts

misconceptions.text: Students change a subscript to make an equation balance, which silently changes the substance instead of conserving atoms.
misconceptions.corrective: Balance only with coefficients; subscripts define the substance and must not change.

examples.text: Burning methane, CH4 + 2 O2 produces CO2 + 2 H2O: one carbon, four hydrogen, and four oxygen atoms appear on each side.

mcBank.stem: A chemical equation is balanced by adjusting coefficients rather than subscripts because
options: balancing with coefficients is only a convenient writing shortcut
changing a subscript would change the identity of the substance
the count of atoms may differ between the two sides
mass is conserved for elements but not for compounds

mapping.inputs: the atoms present in the reactants
mapping.outputs: the atoms present in the products

definition.text: In the circular flow of income, money that households earn returns to firms as spending unless it leaks out of the flow as saving, taxes, or spending on imports.

anchor.quote: money that households earn returns to firms as spending unless it leaks out of the flow as saving, taxes, or spending on imports

facts.text: Leakages are balanced by injections such as investment, government spending, and exports that add spending back into the flow.

anchor.quote: Leakages are balanced by injections such as investment, government spending, and exports that add spending back into the flow

facts.text: When total leakages equal total injections, the circular flow is in balance and national income neither rises nor falls.

anchor.quote: When total leakages equal total injections, the circular flow is in balance and national income neither rises nor falls

misconceptions.text: Students treat saving as money that disappears from the economy rather than a leakage that must be matched by an injection.
misconceptions.corrective: Saving is not destroyed; in balance it re-enters the flow as investment, government spending, or exports.

examples.text: Household saving deposited in a bank is lent to firms as investment, re-injecting money that had leaked out of the flow.
